chunks: And in another report, al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said:

If a woman claims against her husband that he is impotent and the man denies being so, then the ruling in that case is that the man should sit in cold water. If his private part becomes relaxed, then he is impotent; and if it becomes tense, then he is not impotent.

key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal ruling or judicial determination in the case
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the wife or woman making the claim
key_terms.زَوْجِهَا: her husband, against whom the claim is made
key_terms.مَاءٍ بَارِدٍ: cold water, used here as part of the test

ai.seo_question: How is a claim of impotence against a husband judged in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for adjudicating a wife's claim that her husband is impotent when he denies it. It describes a practical test used in resolving the dispute, making the report relevant to marriage law and judicial rulings in Shia fiqh.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4892 - In another narration, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"If a woman accuses her husband of being impotent (ʿinnin) and the man denies it, the ruling in this case is that the man should sit in cold water. If his private part becomes relaxed, then he is indeed impotent. But if it becomes tense, then he is not impotent."
